query: How does goal achievement vary across department, metric, and the management practices described?

per_column.name: management_practice_category
per_column.rationale: Directly named in the query as a dimension of interest; well-separated interpretable categories (technology_investment, process_standardization, etc.) that can be grouped and compared against goal achievement.

per_column.name: improvement_target_type
per_column.rationale: Clear, few, well-balanced categories (satisfaction/volume/time/cost/rate) describing the nature of the goal; an external associational variable that supports meaningful segmentation of achievement.

per_column.name: target_metric_alignment
per_column.rationale: Binary aligned/misaligned split with reasonable balance; highly interpretable and plausibly relates to whether goals are met.

per_column.name: target_scope
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-distributed categories (employee/revenue/customer/efficiency/cost) that segment the goal focus and permit comparison of achievement across scopes.

per_column.name: stakeholder_impact_span
per_column.rationale: Four clear, well-separated categories describing whom the goal affects; a good associational axis for exploring variation in achievement.

per_column.name: risk_or_dependency_indicator
per_column.rationale: Interpretable boolean, but strongly skewed (459 true / 91 false); still usable for comparison though the imbalance limits contrast, so weaker than the others.

per_column.name: comparison_baseline
per_column.rationale: Interpretable baseline categories (prior_year, last_quarter, etc.) that can be grouped and compared; a meaningful associational variable for how targets are framed.

per_column.name: temporal_scope_window
per_column.rationale: Clear, well-separated time-horizon categories enabling segmentation of achievement by timeframe; interpretable and non-constant.

judge.rationale: The set is strongly aligned with the exploratory intent: every column is an external, interpretable, categorical/boolean segmentation variable with well-separated, non-constant values that a human can group on and compare against goal_achievement. Coverage spans the query's explicit axis (management practices) plus complementary framing dimensions (target type, alignment, scope, stakeholder span, baseline, timeframe). None merely restate the focus (goal_achievement itself is not duplicated) and none are opaque scores. Minor weaknesses: risk_or_dependency_indicator is heavily skewed (limiting contrast) and several columns overlap conceptually (scope vs. stakeholder_span vs. target_type), slightly diluting independent informativeness, hence a high but not maximal score.
